summary: Wabash Cannonball is a lean, cutthroat 18xx-lite where every turn is either bidding for a railroad share, building track, or developing a hex, and the constant tension is deciding whether to grab a cheap share now or let someone else overpay for company presidency. Games are tight and fast, with sharp swings from a single well-timed bid or badly placed track tile.
praised: Fast, clean design that teaches 18xx-style stock and track mechanics in under an hour
Meaningful, tense auctions where turn order and bid amount matter enormously
High player interaction and constant decision pressure with almost no downtime
Good gateway into heavier 18xx games without their length or complexity
criticised: Can feel mean or swingy at lower player counts, with runaway leader potential if early auctions go badly
Thin theme; it's an abstract economic engine wearing a railroad skin
Rules and share/dividend interactions take a play or two to click
Map and company set can feel repetitive across sessions

scoring.why: the winner is whoever ends with the most cash after dividends, driven almost entirely by smart share ownership and auction timing
